business_summary.text: Atlanta Electricals manufactures power transformers up to 400kV class across five plants in India, serving state utilities and private customers.

call_points.text: Vadod Unit 4 received Power Grid approval for 400 kV transformers; commercial contribution from next financial year.
Raw material prices under pressure but pass-through via price variation clause; margins expected to sustain at 17-18%.
Export target of 15% of revenue over next three years; no export revenue in Q1FY27.
CRGO steel anti-dumping inquiry initiated; no short-term impact expected, verdict by March 2027.
Chinese players allowed in PSU tenders; no material impact observed yet, monitoring closely.
EBITDA margin expected to remain stable, with 400/765kV products potentially adding around 200 bps once manufactured.
Tank and radiator backward integration capex of ₹170-180 Cr to commence during FY27, with benefits accruing next year.
Exports targeted at 15% of total revenue in three years; first sizeable export order received in FY26.
About 75% of the order book carries a price variation clause, cushioning commodity inflation.
Mineral oil shortage from West Asian conflict affected Q4; mitigated by green transformer production using ester oils.
No data center orders in the order book yet; management sees the opportunity as large but gives no numbers.

guidance.statement: Revenue growth of about 40% CAGR for next 3 years.
Vadod utilisation to reach 65% in FY27 and 100% in FY28.
Net working capital days to rise to 80s-90s in FY27 and FY28.
40% revenue CAGR for next three years
Exports to contribute 15% of revenue in next three years

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Electrical Equipment > Heavy Electrical Equipment

operating_notes.text: FY26 total production across five units was 22,943 MVA.
Vadod unit produced 6,960 MVA in seven months at ~39% utilisation; Ankhi unit produced 580 MVA in Q3FY26.
Order book: ~75% with price variation clause; ~80-85% to execute in FY27.
Order book of ₹3,116.63 Cr as of 30 June 2026; ~₹2,400 Cr executable in FY27.
220 kV class transformers account for over 55% of order book; 400 kV and reactors contribute ~₹275 Cr.
Sales-based capacity utilization of 4,381 MVA in Q1FY27 against installed capacity of 63,060 MVA.

holders.name: HSBC MUTUAL FUND - HSBC MIDCAP FUND

timeline.summary: On 11 May 2026, Atlanta Electricals held its Q4 FY26 earnings call, reporting FY26 revenue of ₹1,851.5 Cr (up 48.8%), PAT of ₹201.8 Cr (up 70.1%), an order book of ₹2,493 Cr, and full repayment of all term loans.
Atlanta Electricals held its Q1FY27 earnings call on 22 July 2026, reporting 48% YoY revenue growth to ₹466.33 Cr and a record order book of ₹3,116.63 Cr.
